note: Names, descriptions and grades are the official PlayStation list as published (Exophase and PSNProfiles agree on all 55). Every guide below is our own advice written from the official description — not yet checked in the game — and says so where a place or step is not pinned down.

sources.official: Official trophy list — Exophase, https://www.exophase.com/game/grand-theft-auto-vi-psn/trophies/ (names, descriptions, grades)
sources.rockstar: Rockstar Games — GTA VI site, rockstargames.com/VI, Trailer 2 (6 May 2025) and the Launch Trailer (15 Oct 2026) (characters Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, Vice City, Leonida and its six regions)
sources.guide: Our own advice, written from the official description for this guide — not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum pops the moment the other 54 trophies are yours — there is nothing extra to do for it. Follow the roadmap in this guide: finish the story, clear every stranger strand and partner trophy before the finale, then work the activity and collectible checklists. Our estimate for the full road is 90–120 hours, in line with GTA V's base-game platinum (200–300 h with its Online trophies; this list has none).
tips: Use the tracker on this page — tick trophies off as you earn them so nothing slips through.
Do the 'watch' trophies (stranger strands, partner trophies, choices) during the story, not after it.
The longest grinds are The Shootist, Cunning Stunts and A Long Road — chip at them between story chapters.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this is the first story trophy you will earn — just play through the start of the game. The mission's name fits Jason's life in the Leonida Keys, where he works for local drug runners out of Brian Heder's boat yard (Rockstar's GTA VI site). Nothing here can be missed; it pops when the mission ends.
tips: Unmissable — awarded for finishing the opening mission.
Take the opening slow: it teaches fishing, driving and the partner system you will use all game.
sources: Rockstar — GTA VI site (Jason, Leonida Keys, Brian Heder)
Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 1 and the trophy pops at the chapter's end. Chapters are the story's big beats, so there is no way to skip past this one. Use Chapter 1 to learn the two-lead system: Lucia and Jason can be switched between, and several trophies later need your partner beside you.
tips: Unmissable story trophy.
Start the stranger strands and side activities as they unlock in Chapter 1 — several later trophies need them finished.
sources: Rockstar — Trailer 2 (Lucia and Jason, two leads)
Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 2 in full. The name is published censored exactly like this on PSN, and we show it as PSN publishes it. Like every chapter trophy it is unmissable — it pops when the last mission of the chapter ends — so the only advice is to keep playing the story and to clear any stranger strands that open up along the way.
tips: Unmissable story trophy.
Check the map for stranger icons after each mission — strands open gradually through the chapters.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 3 and the trophy pops. This is the chapter where the story plants you firmly in Vice City itself — the neon heart of Leonida that both trailers show off — so expect the missions to lean on the city: driving, chases and the partner robberies the game builds toward. Unmissable, like all chapter trophies.
tips: Unmissable story trophy.
Vice City driving is where the stunt and vehicle-discovery counts quietly build — vary your cars.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4, the last chapter before the finale. By now the story has taken Lucia and Jason across Leonida — Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia and Mount Kalaga National Park are the six regions Rockstar named — so before you push into the final mission, sweep up anything flagged 'watch' in this guide: stranger strands, partner trophies and choice trophies may not stay open afterwards.
tips: Unmissable story trophy.
Before the finale: finish every stranger strand and both partner trophies (Hot Together, Retail Therapy).
Check your tracker here — this is the last safe checkpoint.
sources: Rockstar — GTA VI site (six regions of Leonida)
Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Finish the final mission and this gold pops — the story's payoff, and one of only two golds on the list. The description says nothing about a branching ending, and unlike GTA V (where two of the three endings killed a lead and locked four trophies) there is no official word of a choice at the end of GTA VI, so we do not claim one. What we do know: finish the stranger strands and partner trophies first, because a finale is the one point in any GTA where side content can close.
tips: Gold — the story finale.
Clear all 'watch' trophies before starting the final mission.
GTA V's lesson: in that game the Deathwish ending protected the missables. GTA VI publishes no such choice, so do not assume one exists.
sources: GTA V trophy structure — 6 missables, Deathwish ending (gametree.me / pixelforgeguides.com)
Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run. Named story missions like this one are unmissable — they sit on the main path, and the trophy pops when the mission ends. The title suggests an early job for Brian Heder's crew in the Keys, but the mission itself is only named in the official trophy description, so treat any detail beyond that as unconfirmed until you play it.
tips: Unmissable story mission.
Named-mission trophies (ids 8–13) all work the same way: play the story, collect them in order.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heists are the set-pieces GTA is built around — Trailer 2's premise is a job that goes wrong and drags Lucia and Jason into a conspiracy across Leonida — so expect a multi-stage mission with a getaway. It is on the main path and cannot be missed; the trophy pops at the mission's end.
tips: Unmissable story mission.
Heist missions are good places to practise Combat Focus — you will need it for Gunslinger later.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play. The title points at Lucia's family — she landed in prison fighting for hers, per Rockstar's own bio — but the mission's contents are not public beyond its name in the official description. It is a main-path mission, so it is unmissable: play the story and it pops.
tips: Unmissable story mission.
If a mission ever feels hard, remember GTA lets you retry from checkpoints — story trophies never depend on doing it perfectly.
sources: Rockstar — GTA VI site (Lucia Caminos bio)
Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. The name ties to Leonida's music scene — Dre'Quan Priest books acts for Boobie Ike's club and Real Dimez are the rap duo turning street life into tracks — so expect this one to run through Vice City's nightlife. It is on the main path and unmissable; the trophy pops when the mission ends.
tips: Unmissable story mission.
Nightclub and street missions are a good time to work on the WAiNK It and vehicle-discovery counts.
sources: Rockstar — GTA VI site (Dre'Quan Priest, Real Dimez, Boobie Ike)
Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown, set at Vice City International Airport — the same airport behind the 'unscheduled departure' trophy (Catch Me If You Can). A takedown at the airport suggests a hijack or interception job, and it is a main-path mission, so it is unmissable. Finish it and the trophy pops.
tips: Unmissable story mission.
While you are at VCIA, remember Catch Me If You Can — an unscheduled departure from the airport is its own trophy.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. The military-sounding name and Jason's army past (discharged before the story opens, per the Launch Trailer) point at a heavy combat mission, possibly with the Rhino tanks behind Challenging Tank. It is main-path and unmissable — the trophy pops at the mission's end — so go in with full armour and ammo and use cover.
tips: Unmissable story mission.
Stock up on armour and heavy weapons before military-style missions.
Tanks appear in this stretch of the game — note how they behave for Challenging Tank.
sources: Rockstar — Launch Trailer (15 Oct 2026, Jason's army past)
Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion — the second gold on the list and, like GTA V's Career Criminal, the trophy that only pops when everything else is done. In GTA V, 100% meant the story plus a fixed checklist of Strangers & Freaks, hobbies, random events and collectibles; GTA VI's exact checklist is not published yet, so use this guide's tracker as your working list: every activity, collectible and strand trophy below is very likely part of it. Check the in-game stats page regularly to see what the game itself counts.
tips: Gold — the 100% trophy.
Keep this guide's tracker at 100% and the in-game stats page will agree with it — or tell you what is missing.
Save the grind trophies (stunts, shooting range, cards) for after the story, when the whole map is open.
sources: GTA V 100% structure — story + Strangers & Freaks + hobbies + collectibles (pixelforgeguides.com)
Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts — jumps, near misses, drifts, air time, whatever the game counts as a stunt. GTA V had 50 stunt jumps as a fixed checklist; GTA VI counts 250 stunts as a running total instead, so this is a grind you build up by driving boldly everywhere rather than a list to tick off one by one. Use fast cars on Vice City's highways and the long bridges out of the city, chain jumps off ramps, and let it accumulate during normal play before you grind the remainder.
tips: Silver — a running total, not a fixed checklist.
Drive fast and take jumps during every trip; the count builds in the background.
For the last stretch, find a good ramp and repeat it — stunts repeat, locations do not need to be unique.
sources: GTA V stunt structure — 50 stunt jumps (pixelforgeguides.com)
Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each type of activity once — PSN's target is 9 activity types. The activities the trophies name give you the list to work from: shooting range, drone racing, racing, fishing, arcade games, bowling, meditation and hunting, plus at least one more the descriptions do not name (the game's phone apps and the Extended Look's club and robbery activities are candidates). Work through the named ones first — each has its own trophy — and the ninth will reveal itself in the activities menu.
tips: PSN target: 9 activity types.
Every activity trophy in this guide is one of the nine — finish them and this pops along the way.
Check the in-game activities list for any type you have not tried.
sources: Rockstar — An Extended Look (27 Aug 2026, activities shown)
Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges (PSN target). This is the hardest skill trophy on the list and the closest thing GTA VI has to GTA V's Solid Gold, Baby! (70 gold medals) — expect tight time limits and accuracy gates that need practice, not luck. Work through the ranges weapon by weapon, learn each challenge's par, and use the range's own retry — golds are per challenge, so a bad run costs you nothing but time.
tips: Silver — 42 gold medals, the hardest skill trophy here.
Do a few ranges between story missions so the skill builds gradually.
If a challenge gates on a weapon you rarely use, practise that weapon in free roam first.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations (PSN target). Top Fun is the returning drone-racing brand, and each location is a separate race to win — the trophy needs a win at every one, not just 14 wins anywhere. Learn each course's line before you race it for real, and remember drone races are about smooth lines and throttle control, not top speed.
tips: PSN target: 14 locations, a win at each.
Race each location once to learn it, then go for the win.
Drone races are repeatable, so a loss costs nothing.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — the word 'different' matters, so the same race won twice counts once. Races are one of the activities the Extended Look shows, and the map offers street, off-road and water races across Leonida's six regions. Work through the race list region by region, and use the fastest car you own for each surface; a race you lose can be retried immediately.
tips: 20 different races — repeats do not count.
Tick them off region by region so you can see which are left.
Winning also pays, which helps Treat Yo Self and the garage fund.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal Hampton in a fishing challenge. Cal is Jason's friend — the one who spends his nights listening to Coast Guard radio with a few beers, per Rockstar's bio — and fishing is the activity that opens the game (Gone Fishing). Find Cal, take his challenge, and out-fish him: the challenge is a head-to-head, so it is about landing more or bigger fish than he does, not about a fixed score. If you lose, challenge him again.
tips: Fish with Cal as soon as his challenge appears — it is repeatable.
Fishing also builds toward the 100% checklist, so practise the casting and reeling timing early.
sources: Rockstar — GTA VI site (Cal Hampton bio)
Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game — finish it, not just start it. Arcade cabinets sit in bars and clubs around Vice City (the nightlife the trailers lean on), and the game will count a full playthrough of any one cabinet. Pick the cabinet whose game you find easiest, learn its controls in a practice run, then play it through to the end.
tips: Any one arcade game, played to completion.
If a cabinet's game is hard, try another — the trophy only needs one.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.missableNote: Stranger strands may close after story beats. Finish Andy's strand as soon as it unlocks — do not leave it until after the finale.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Andy's stranger strand. Stranger missions are the side stories GTA V called Strangers & Freaks — in GTA VI the trophy is Strangers & Freaks again, and it needs 8 strands finished. Andy is one of the strangers you meet across Leonida; follow his strand to its last mission. The official description does not say whether strands stay open after the finale, so treat this as 'do it when it unlocks' and finish it before the final mission.
tips: WATCH — finish this strand during the story, not after it.
Stranger icons appear on the map as you explore — check new regions as they open.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.missableNote: Stranger strands may close after story beats. Finish Kenton's strand as soon as it unlocks — do not leave it until after the finale.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Kenton's stranger strand. The title is a boating joke, and Kenton's strand most likely runs through the Leonida Keys or the Grassrivers — the water country around Vice City. Like every strand trophy, the safe play is to follow it to its end as soon as it opens, because the official descriptions do not promise strands stay available after the story ends.
tips: WATCH — finish this strand during the story, not after it.
Boat missions are a good time to work on vehicle discovery — try different boats.
sources: Rockstar — GTA VI site (Leonida Keys, Grassrivers)
Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.missableNote: Stranger strands may close after story beats. Finish Billy's strand as soon as it unlocks — do not leave it until after the finale.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Billy's stranger strand. 'The Lone Rider' points at bikes, so expect this strand to run through Leonida's biker country — Port Gellhorn or the roads around Mount Kalaga are the rural corners Rockstar named. Follow the strand to its last mission as soon as it unlocks; like the other strand trophies, do not gamble on it staying open after the finale.
tips: WATCH — finish this strand during the story, not after it.
Biker missions are a natural place to practise stunts for Cunning Stunts.
sources: Rockstar — GTA VI site (Port Gellhorn, Mount Kalaga)
Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.missableNote: Needs 8 full strands. Strands may close after story beats — start each one as it unlocks and finish it before the finale.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 full mission strands for strangers across Leonida. Five of the strangers have their own trophies — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone — so those five are your first five strands, and three more strangers are still to be found by exploring. In GTA V the equivalent was 20 Strangers & Freaks for 100%; here it is 8 complete strands, which makes each one longer and more story-like. Start every strand the moment its icon appears and finish it before the finale.
tips: Silver — 8 complete strands.
The five named strangers (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) are strands 1–5 — find three more by exploring.
Strands unlock across all six regions, so explore as the map opens.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.missableNote: Stranger strands may close after story beats. Finish Randy's strand as soon as it unlocks — do not leave it until after the finale.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Randy's stranger strand. The name is pure supply-chain crime — moving product through Leonida — and the strand will likely run through the Keys' smuggling routes or Vice City's dealers. Follow it to its last mission as soon as it opens, and do not leave it for after the finale: the official descriptions do not promise strands stay open.
tips: WATCH — finish this strand during the story, not after it.
Smuggling strands often involve boats and planes — both count toward vehicle discovery.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.missableNote: Stranger strands may close after story beats. Finish Tyrone's strand as soon as it unlocks — do not leave it until after the finale.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of Tyrone's stranger strand. 'Spin On This!' sounds like a DJ or club strand — Vice City's music scene again, where Dre'Quan books acts and Real Dimez play — so expect this one to run through the clubs. Finish it as soon as it unlocks; like the other strand trophies, the safe window is during the story.
tips: WATCH — finish this strand during the story, not after it.
Club strands are a good time to work on the WAiNK It count around Vice City.
sources: Rockstar — GTA VI site (Dre'Quan Priest, Real Dimez)
Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 spots across Leonida (PSN target). Meditation spots are quiet places — beaches, hilltops, the edges of Mount Kalaga National Park — and each one is a short sit-down, not a challenge. The exact 18 spots are not published, so work region by region: the spots are spread across all six regions Rockstar named, and the count in your tracker will tell you how many are left in each area as you find them.
tips: PSN target: 18 spots.
Explore region by region — Vice City, Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, Mount Kalaga.
Meditation spots never expire, so save the hunt for after the story if you like.
sources: Rockstar — GTA VI site (six regions of Leonida)
Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt one unique animal for Bret. Bret is a stranger who wants a specific animal — the Grassrivers (Leonida's swamp country) and Mount Kalaga National Park are the wild places Rockstar named, and a unique animal means a one-of-a-kind target, not just any deer or boar. Take a scoped rifle, track the animal Bret describes, and take the shot cleanly; the hunt is repeatable if you miss.
tips: One unique animal, for Bret — not regular hunting.
Use a scoped rifle and approach downwind; unique animals are usually wary.
The Grassrivers and Mount Kalaga are the likeliest hunting grounds.
sources: Rockstar — GTA VI site (Grassrivers, Mount Kalaga National Park)
Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 full collectible card sets. Cards are scattered across Leonida — shops, bars, hidden spots — and a 'set' is a complete group of cards, so you need every card in three sets, not just three cards. GTA's collectibles have always rewarded the player who searches every corner: check shops and interiors as you pass them, and save a dedicated sweep for after the story when the whole map is open.
tips: Silver — 3 complete sets.
Pick up cards whenever you see them; do not leave them for later.
A dedicated post-story sweep is the fastest way to finish the last set.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK It feature at 100 locations. WAiNK is one of the game's phone apps — the Extended Look shows phone apps as a core system — and 'WAiNK It' reads like a check-in or photo-tag at a place: open the app at a named location and tag it. The count is a running total across Leonida, so tag everywhere you go during normal play and the last stretch is a short tour of places you have not tagged yet.
tips: Silver — 100 locations.
Open WAiNK at every new place you visit — the count builds passively.
Mop up the last tags with a tour of the six regions.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges — the game's rolling list of small feats, from driving and shooting to exploring and earning. Challenges are the connective tissue between the other trophies: stunts, races, robberies and discoveries all feed the challenge list, so this trophy mostly pops on its own if you play broadly. If it stalls, open the challenges menu and pick the easiest unfinished ones.
tips: 50 challenges — a running total.
Play broadly: every other trophy feeds this one.
The challenges menu shows exactly which are left — farm the easiest.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.missableNote: Needs your partner beside you. Do it during the story while partner missions are frequent — do not leave it for after the finale.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level and then lose it and escape. The Heat system is the new police system the Extended Look shows, and 4 stars means helicopters and heavy response — so pick your moment: get the wanted level with Lucia or Jason at your side, then break line of sight, switch cars, and hide until the stars clear. The trophy pops when you escape, not when you earn the stars.
tips: WATCH — needs your partner beside you.
Break line of sight, ditch the car, hide — do not try to outrun helicopters.
Partner missions are the easiest time to have your partner with you.
sources: Rockstar — An Extended Look (Heat police system)
Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.missableNote: Needs your partner beside you and three shops in a row. Do it during the story while partner missions are frequent.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob 3 shops back-to-back without losing your wanted level — the trick is the 'without losing' part: you must keep the heat alive across all three robberies. Plan a route of three close shops in Vice City, hit them fast one after another, and keep moving so the police stay on you but never catch you. If the stars clear between shops, the chain breaks and you start over.
tips: WATCH — needs your partner beside you.
Pick three shops on one street and hit them in order, fast.
Keep moving between shops — if the wanted level clears, the chain resets.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles — get in and drive (or at least register) 100 different vehicles across Leonida. 'Discover' means new to your collection, so a car you have already driven does not count twice. Variety is the strategy: cars, bikes, boats, planes and trucks, in the city and out in the country. The vehicle list fills itself during normal play if you keep switching rides instead of using one favourite car.
tips: 100 different vehicles.
Switch rides constantly — every new vehicle counts.
Boats, planes and bikes count too, not just cars.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in one use of Combat Focus — the game's slow-mo aiming mode. The setup matters more than the aim: find a spot with at least five enemies grouped together (a gang hideout or a story shootout), trigger Combat Focus, and drop five before the meter runs out. If the meter ends at four, just retry — Combat Focus recharges, and the trophy only needs one clean run.
tips: Five takedowns, one Combat Focus use.
Pick a fight with five or more enemies close together.
Story shootouts with grouped enemies are the easiest setup.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at Vice City International Airport — steal a plane and take off without filing a flight plan, in other words. Get onto the VCIA tarmac (the airport from the VCIA Takedown mission), take any plane, and get airborne; expect a wanted level the moment you do, so take off fast and climb away from the airport. Any plane works — the trophy is about the departure, not the aircraft.
tips: Any plane, any runway — just take off unscheduled.
Expect police attention the moment you roll.
You already visit VCIA for the Takedown mission — do this on the same trip if you can.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The description is a joke — 'Kinda hot in these Rhinos' — and the Rhino is GTA's tank, so this trophy is about tanks: most likely driving one, surviving in one, or taking one on. The military mission Operation Savage Glory is where tanks show up in the story, so pay attention there: if a Rhino is driveable in that mission, drive it; if you have to fight one, use sticky bombs or heavy weapons and keep moving. The exact trigger is not published, so try the obvious tank interaction first and check the trophy list after.
tips: About the Rhino tank — the exact trigger is not published yet.
Operation Savage Glory is the likeliest place tanks appear.
If driving one does not pop it, try destroying one — and report what worked.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description — exact trigger not yet pinned down

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — a clean stealth job, not a smash-and-grab. Case the store first: learn the guard patrols and the camera positions, go in quiet, take the goods and leave before anyone raises the alarm. If you are spotted, the attempt fails — leave, let the heat die down, and try again with a better route. A suppressed weapon and patience beat speed here.
tips: Undetected is the whole trophy — one alarm and the attempt fails.
Scout the store first: guards, cameras, exits.
Leave quietly the moment you have the goods — do not linger.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape from each one. Bank vaults are the big robberies — Raul Bautista is the seasoned bank robber Rockstar profiled, and his jobs are the model for these — so each vault is a planned hit with a getaway, not a quick shop robbery. Five vaults, five clean escapes: plan the getaway before you go in, bring your partner where the job allows it, and do not get greedy once the vault is open.
tips: Silver — 5 vaults, 5 escapes.
Plan the getaway first, the robbery second.
Raul Bautista's story jobs teach the bank-robbery pattern — do those first.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob one armored truck and escape. Armored trucks run set routes around Vice City — spot one, stop it (ram it, block it, or hit the driver), crack it open and take the cash, then lose the wanted level. The name nods to GTA V's Blitz Play heist, and the method is the same shape: stop the truck, grab the money, vanish. One clean escape is all it takes.
tips: One truck, one escape.
Block the truck's route rather than chasing it at speed.
Have a fast getaway car parked nearby before you strike.
sources: GTA V — Blitz Play heist structure (grandtheftwiki.com)
Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida (PSN target) — every named place on the map, from Vice City's neighbourhoods to the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia and Mount Kalaga National Park. In GTA V the same trophy (San Andreas Sightseer) needed every corner of the map visited; here the count is 52 areas, and the map itself shows which are left. Drive, fly and sail through them all — a plane tour after the story is the fastest way to mop up the last few.
tips: PSN target: 52 areas.
The map tracks what you have visited — check it region by region.
A post-story plane tour finishes the last areas fast.
sources: Rockstar — GTA VI site (six regions of Leonida)
Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs (PSN target). Each gang runs its own racket somewhere in Leonida — a stash house, a deal, a chop shop — and you need to hit one operation per gang, all nine. The gangs are spread across the map, so this is really an exploration trophy in a robbery's clothes: find each gang's turf, hit its operation, and move on to the next.
tips: PSN target: 9 gangs, one operation each.
Learn each gang's turf as you explore — the operations sit on their ground.
Hit-and-run: take the goods and leave before reinforcements arrive.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Go to Ocean Beach in Vice City, order a cocktail, and enjoy the view. Ocean Beach is the beachfront strip — the Miami Beach of Vice City, and the first place Trailer 1 showed — so find a bar with a sea view, sit down, and order. The ellipsis in the name is a nod to the beginning of the series' Vice City story, and the trophy is a pure breather: no challenge, just a drink with a view.
tips: Ocean Beach, Vice City — any bar with a sea view.
The easiest trophy on the list: sit, order, done.
Do it early — it is a nice palate cleanser between missions.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Drive a car through a vehicle showroom's window and out the other side — the classic GTA showroom smash, in the style of the old games. Pick any vehicle showroom in Vice City, get a car up to speed, and drive straight through the glass. The trophy is about the exit, so keep going until you are out on the street; the damage to the car is the point.
tips: Any showroom, any car — speed and a straight line.
Expect a wanted level; the trophy pops on the exit, so do not stop.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Bowl at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley — follow through on a full game. The name is a wink at GTA IV's famous bowling dates, and the alley is a named place in Vice City, so find Kolt & Associates on the map, rent a lane, and play a game through. You do not need a high score: the trophy is for playing, not winning.
tips: Kolt & Associates bowling alley, Vice City.
Play a full game — score does not matter.
Bowling counts as one of the 9 activity types for Master of None.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: The description is deliberately vague — 'a partnership with mass appeal' — and that vagueness is the point: this is a story or social-media moment for Lucia and Jason's partnership, most likely tied to Real Dimez and the social-media fame the trailers show (the duo turn street life into tracks and posts). It will almost certainly pop on its own as you play the story's partnership beats, so do not hunt for it: play the missions, do the partner activities, and it will come.
tips: Likely a story beat — expect it to pop during normal play.
If it has not popped by the finale, check the partner and social activities (Real Dimez, WAiNK).
sources: Rockstar — GTA VI site (Real Dimez, social media)
Guide: our own advice from the official description — exact trigger not yet pinned down

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.missableNote: PSN tracks a count to 500 choices. Make choices whenever the game offers them — some may not come back.
trophies.guide: Make choices — PSN tracks a count to 500 of them. GTA VI offers choices through the story and the open world (dialogue options, approach choices, side decisions), and this trophy counts them up. The practical advice is simple: never skip a choice when the game offers one, and take the decision that fits your playthrough rather than always picking the same answer. The count builds across the whole game, so this is a background trophy, not a grind.
tips: WATCH — PSN target: 500 choices.
Take every choice the game offers, in missions and in free roam.
Choices may not repeat, so do not skip them.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: 'Second time's the charm' — this trophy is about succeeding on a second attempt. The most natural reading is retrying something you failed once: a mission, a challenge, a race, a stunt. It will very likely pop on its own the first time you retry and pass something, so do not force it: play normally, and when you fail anything, try it again right away instead of moving on.
tips: Retry anything you fail — the second attempt is the point.
Expect this to pop naturally during the story.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description — exact trigger not yet pinned down

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: 'What the hell just happened?' — this is GTA's classic 'witness something strange' trophy, in the line of GTA V's Out of Your Depth (get attacked by a shark). Leonida is full of weird encounters: UFOs, swamp creatures, strange NPCs, the Grassrivers at night. Explore the odd corners of the map — the swamps, the Keys, the deserted stretches — and something strange will find you. It pops when it happens, so the only method is to keep exploring.
tips: Explore strange places: Grassrivers, the Keys, remote roads at night.
Random encounters are the trigger — keep playing and it will find you.
sources: GTA V — Out of Your Depth (grandtheftwiki.com)
Guide: our own advice from the official description — exact trigger not yet pinned down

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone over with a melee drive-by — hit a pedestrian with a melee weapon while driving past. The bowling pun is the joke: you are the ball, they are the pin. Get a car up to speed on a busy Vice City street, lean out with a melee weapon (a bat works), and clip a pedestrian as you pass. It is deliberately silly and easy to set up in traffic; one clean hit pops it.
tips: A melee weapon, a moving car, a pedestrian — one hit.
Busy Vice City streets give you the most targets.
This is the combat cousin of the bowling trophy — do both in one session.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills are the dirty money from robberies — the heists and vault jobs pay in bills you cannot spend directly — and your contacts clean them for a cut. The money builds up from the robberies you are already doing for other trophies (vaults, armored trucks, gang operations), so launder regularly through your contacts instead of letting marked bills pile up, and the $250,000 will come.
tips: Launder after every big robbery — do not let marked bills sit.
Vaults and armored trucks are the biggest sources of marked bills.
The $250,000 is earnings, so keep laundering until the total hits it.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — clothes, weapons, car mods, food, anything the shops sell. This is the easiest money trophy on the list because spending is something you do anyway: weapons and ammo for the hard missions, car upgrades for the races, clothes for the fun of it. If you reach the endgame short of the total, buy the most expensive things you have not bought yet — a top-end car or a full weapon loadout closes the gap fast.
tips: Spend normally and this pops on its own.
Car mods and weapons are the fastest way to close a gap.
Counts across all shops, so every purchase helps.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties (PSN target). Garages are the properties that store your vehicle collection — and with 100 vehicles to discover, you will need the space. Garages go on sale as you progress and cost serious money, so save for them through the story and buy them as they unlock; the last one is usually the most expensive, so keep a reserve. The trophy pops when the eighth deed is yours.
tips: PSN target: 8 garage properties.
Buy garages as they unlock — do not leave them all for the end.
Garages also store the 100 vehicles for Whip It Good, so they pay for themselves.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — the game's vehicle-sharing app, one of the phone apps the Extended Look shows. Scooter Bros is Leonida's ride-share, and registering a vehicle means adding a car or bike you own (or have found) to the app so it can be called up. Register ten different vehicles — variety helps, and the cars you discover for Whip It Good are the obvious candidates — and the trophy pops on the tenth.
tips: 10 different vehicles registered.
Register the cars you discover for Whip It Good — the two trophies feed each other.
The app is on the in-game phone — check it whenever you get a new ride.
sources: Guide: our own advice from the official description
